preconditions.expression: all(len(alarm) == 5 and alarm[2] == ':' and alarm[0:2].isdigit() and alarm[3:5].isdigit() for alarm in alarms)
preconditions.description: Each alarm time is a string of length 5 in the format 'HH:MM', where HH and MM are digits.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(alarm[0:2]) <= 23 and 0 <= int(alarm[3:5]) <= 59 for alarm in alarms)
preconditions.description: Each alarm time represents a valid time of day (HH:MM), where HH is between 00 and 23 and MM is between 00 and 59.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '00:00' or (return_value != '00:00' and all(0 <= int(return_value[0:2]) <= 23 and 0 <= int(return_value[3:5]) <= 59))
postconditions.description: The result is a valid time string in 'HH:MM' format, where HH is between 00 and 23 and MM is between 00 and 59, or '00:00' if no alarms are provided.
If there is only one unique alarm at '00:00', the result is '00:00'.
If there is only one unique alarm (not '00:00'), the result is '00:00' (the interval wraps around midnight).

postconditions.expression: len(set(alarms)) > 1 and return_value == max((((int(alarm1[0:2]) * 60 + int(alarm1[3:5])) - (int(alarm2[0:2]) * 60 + int(alarm2[3:5]))) % 1440 for alarm1 in set(alarms) for alarm2 in set(alarms) if alarm1 != alarm2), key=lambda x: x) % 1440)
postconditions.description: The result is the maximum time interval (in minutes) between any two distinct alarms in the set, formatted as 'HH:MM'. The interval is calculated as the difference between two alarms, wrapping around midnight if necessary.
